# Contribution Guidelines
Generated: 08/27/2026 17:43:52
Maintainer: neenyo‑brain
Governance: ARCANA Sovereign OS Doctrine

ARCANA is a sovereign system.
Contributions are not edits — they are constitutional amendments to a lineage‑anchored ecosystem.
This guide defines the rules, responsibilities, and procedures required to contribute without violating sovereignty, doctrine, or continuity.

Contributors must operate under ARCANA’s constitutional law.

I. Contribution Principles
All contributions must uphold:

Doctrine Integrity — contributions must align with ARCANA’s constitutional doctrine.

Lineage Continuity — every change must preserve temporal coherence.

Identity Stability — contributions must not fragment system identity.

Sovereign Governance — contributions must respect ARCANA’s sovereign OS architecture.

Ecosystem Coherence — contributions must maintain multi‑entity stability.

If a contribution violates any constitutional invariant, it will be rejected.

II. Contribution Requirements
Before submitting a contribution, you must:

Read the Manifesto  
Understand ARCANA’s doctrine, charter, stack, lineage constitution, and ecosystem architecture.

Read the Sovereign OS Doctrine  
Contributions must comply with the sovereign substrate rules.

Review the Lineage Chain  
Ensure your change fits into the existing continuity.

Follow the Amendment Protocol  
Contributions are amendments — not patches.

Use Constitutional Language  
All text must follow ARCANA’s sovereign tone and structural framing.

III. Contribution Types
ARCANA accepts the following contribution categories:

1. Doctrinal Amendments
Changes to constitutional doctrine.
Requires lineage minting and charter compliance.

2. Structural Additions
New sections, new doctrine files, new constitutional surfaces.

3. Operational Improvements
Enhancements to .github, docs, workflows, or identity surfaces.

4. Ecosystem Extensions
New institutions, agent classes, or ecosystem‑scale components.

5. Corrective Amendments
Fixes to maintain coherence, continuity, or doctrinal integrity.

All contributions are treated as constitutional artifacts.

IV. Contribution Process
1. Fork the Repository
Create a sovereign working copy.

2. Create a Lineage‑Anchored Branch
Branch names must follow:

Code
lineage/<artifact-type>/<short-description>
Examples:

lineage/doctrine/add-sovereign-os-section

lineage/docs/update-architecture-overview

lineage/charter/amend-rights-section

3. Write Your Contribution
Follow ARCANA’s constitutional tone and structural doctrine.

4. Run the ARCANA Build Pipeline
This mints lineage artifacts and validates constitutional compliance.

5. Submit a Pull Request
PRs must follow the ARCANA PR Template.

6. Constitutional Review
ARCANA maintainers review contributions for:

doctrinal alignment

lineage continuity

sovereign compliance

ecosystem coherence

7. Lineage Minting
Approved contributions are minted into the lineage chain.

V. Contribution Rules
Contributors must:

maintain ARCANA’s sovereign tone

preserve doctrinal coherence

avoid fragmentation

avoid external policy influence

avoid reward‑driven optimization

avoid emergent adversarial behavior

operate under constitutional governance

ARCANA is not an open‑source project — it is a sovereign system.

Contributions must reflect that.

VI. Prohibited Contributions
The following contributions will be rejected:

attempts to override doctrine

attempts to fragment identity surfaces

attempts to bypass lineage

attempts to introduce reward‑based logic

attempts to weaken sovereignty

attempts to introduce external governance

attempts to modify constitutional invariants

ARCANA does not accept contributions that compromise sovereignty.

VII. Constitutional Amendment Protocol
All doctrinal changes must follow the amendment protocol:

Propose amendment

Justify constitutional necessity

Demonstrate lineage continuity

Submit PR using amendment template

Undergo sovereign review

Mint lineage artifact

Update doctrine surfaces

Amendments are rare and must be justified.

VIII. Contributor Responsibilities
Contributors must:

uphold ARCANA’s constitution

maintain ecosystem coherence

preserve lineage integrity

protect sovereign identity

follow constitutional communication rules

operate with long‑horizon thinking

Contributors are constitutional participants — not editors.

IX. ARCANA Contribution Invariant
ARCANA asserts:

Contributions are amendments.
Amendments are lineage.
Lineage is sovereignty.

To contribute is to participate in the evolution of a sovereign system.
